name: Employees
definition: The headcount of people directly employed by the utility, expressed as a number of employees. It counts permanent full-time and part-time staff on the payroll, and excludes contractors, consultants and other outsourced labour. The headcount is sliced by division and by gender through separate dimensions, which supports PPA gender-representation reporting; note that headcount treats a part-time person the same as a full-time one, so it will read higher than the equivalent full-time-equivalent (FTE) figure.

name: FTE Employees
definition: The size of the utility's workforce expressed in full-time equivalents (FTE), where each unit represents one full-time working schedule. Permanent full-time and part-time staff on the payroll are converted to FTE on the basis of hours worked, so that two half-time employees count as one FTE; contractors and consultants are excluded. Unlike a plain headcount, FTE reflects the true labour capacity of the utility and is the appropriate denominator for productivity ratios such as customers or connections per employee.

name: Hours lost to Work Related Injuries
definition: The total number of working hours lost as a result of work-related injuries during the period, expressed in hours. It captures time an employee would otherwise have worked but could not because of a lost-time injury sustained on the job, following standard occupational health and safety (OHS) conventions; it excludes absence unrelated to workplace injury such as ordinary sick leave or annual leave. The figure feeds injury-severity and lost-time measures, so consistent counting of the first day off and of partial days is important for comparability across utilities.

name: Hours Worked Standard
definition: The standard, or rostered, number of working hours for the utility's staff over the period, expressed in hours. It represents the contracted or scheduled hours that employees would work under normal conditions, before any overtime, absence or leave is taken into account. Used together with actual and paid hours, it forms the baseline for staff-utilisation measures; because it is a scheduled figure rather than a recorded one, it should reflect the standard working week applied consistently across the workforce.

name: Hours Worked Actual
definition: The actual number of hours worked by the utility's staff over the period, expressed in hours. It records time genuinely spent working, including overtime and excluding hours paid but not worked such as leave or public holidays. Compared against standard and paid hours it drives staff-utilisation and productivity measures, so overtime and time-recording practices should be captured consistently to keep the ratios meaningful.

name: Hours Paid
definition: The total number of hours the utility paid its staff for over the period, expressed in hours. It includes hours actually worked as well as paid time not worked, such as annual leave, sick leave and public holidays, but excludes unpaid absence. Set against actual and standard hours, it underpins staff-utilisation measures; the gap between hours paid and hours worked is a useful signal of leave and absence loading, so the two should be recorded on a consistent basis.

name: Number of Work Related Injuries
definition: The count of work-related injuries recorded during the period, expressed as a number of incidents. Following standard occupational health and safety (OHS) conventions it covers injuries arising out of the course of employment, typically those serious enough to be reported or to result in lost time, and excludes non-work-related or off-duty injuries. Because utilities differ in size, this raw count is usually read alongside hours worked as a frequency rate per million hours; small workforces produce small counts, so year-on-year swings can look large in relative terms.

name: Gender
definition: An option-typed attribute that records the gender of an employee or role, selected from the platform's standard Gender list rather than entered as a number. It classifies workforce records so that headcount and other HR measures can be sliced by gender through a dimension. Consistent use of the same gender categories across all utilities is what makes the resulting gender-representation reporting to the PPA comparable.
